subject: Discrepancy on AWS Marketplace invoice — July credits not applied

From: Jenny Park <billing@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy on AWS Marketplace invoice — July credits not applied

Hi Rishi,

We noticed an unexpected shortfall on our July AWS Marketplace invoice (Invoice #AMZ-2028-07-1192). Several usage lines that were marked as pre-applied credits in our seller portal did not appear as credit lines on the invoice we received on 7/29. The delta is ~US$18,640 and it looks tied to three SKU lines that should have been zeroed due to a prior settlement.

Can you help trace whether Redwood is seeing the same ledger signals from AWS? If this is an invoicing-side issue we need to escalate quickly: our finance team requires the corrected credit memo by the end of the month to avoid payment hold.

I attached a CSV export from our billing UI showing the expected credits and the matching AWS line IDs.

Thanks,
Jenny Park
Billing Manager
Acme Analytics
attachments: acme_aws_invoice_202807.csv (csv)

Hi Jenny — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. I pulled the invoice PDF you mentioned and started a quick match to our usage signals. A couple quick asks so we can triage:

- Can you confirm whether the credits were issued by AWS marketplace seller ops (i.e., an AWS credit memo) or applied via your account-level adjustment?
- If you have the seller's credit memo ID (or Marketplace adjustment ID) include that in a follow-up.

Internally I've looped in Marcus from Finance and Laura from Sales. Marcus — can you take an initial look at the CSV and our meter-side logs to see whether the three SKUs reconcile to Redwood's reported usage? If we confirm a mismatch we'll open a ticket with Marketplace Support and request a credit memo / corrected invoice.

I'll also route to AWS contacts once we have the consolidated matrix.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi — thanks for the quick reply. The credits were issued by the seller (Acme Analytics) via a marketplace adjustment request (SellerAdj-ID: SADJ-7721). I do not see an AWS-level credit memo attached to the invoice PDF.

Attached is the CSV (same file): three invoice line item IDs are 4221-07-A, 4221-07-B, 4221-07-C. The seller portal shows 0.00 for those lines after the adjustment. I also included our VAT breakout column in the CSV — for clarity, the adjustment should not change VAT treatment.

Our preferred outcome: corrected invoice or a credit memo that we can apply to our AR, and confirmation that Redwood's uplifts (if any) are aligned so we don't have double-charge exposure.

Thanks,
Jenny

Subject: RE: Discrepancy on AWS Marketplace invoice — July credits not applied

Following up with an initial analysis — I pulled our meter logs and matched against Jenny's CSV. Summary:

- Two of the three SKUs (4221-07-A, 4221-07-B) appear in our usage ledger with timestamps and token counts that match Acme's export. No duplication on our side.
- SKU 4221-07-C shows a sequence gap where we pushed an upstream retry during the billing window; our runtime aggregated event for that window reports a transient duplication that was later deduplicated by our batcher. The marketplace line appears to have been zeroed on Acme's portal but AWS invoiced the original aggregated token run before the seller adjustment propagated.

Proposed next steps (short list):
1) Compile a reconciliation matrix (attached) that maps AWS invoice line IDs to Redwood usage IDs and timestamps.
2) Request AWS Marketplace Support to issue a credit memo for Invoice AMZ-2028-07-1192 for the delta (approx US$18,640).
3) Ask Acme to confirm SellerAdj-ID SADJ-7721 records (they supplied it) and share any marketplace ticket ID they received.

I've attached a working worksheet: metering_match_matrix.xlsx. Laura — can you confirm if Sales wants to offer a limited goodwill credit until this is fully resolved? We should avoid altering AR until AWS issues the credit memo.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
attachments: metering_match_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Request: credit memo issuance for Invoice AMZ-2028-07-1192 (trace attached)

Hello Marketplace Support / Simon,

We're opening a request on behalf of our mutual customer (Acme Analytics) regarding Invoice AMZ-2028-07-1192. Acme submitted SellerAdj-ID SADJ-7721 which should have zeroed three invoice line items (4221-07-A/B/C). Acme's portal shows the adjustment but the invoice PDF delivered to them and the billed amount in AWS invoicing do not reflect the seller adjustment.

What we've attached:
- metering_match_matrix.xlsx: mapping between AWS invoice line IDs, Redwood usage record IDs, and timestamps (rows flagged where mismatch observed).
- acme_aws_invoice_202807.csv: Acme's export showing expected zeroed lines and VAT breakout.

Requested action:
- Confirm whether SADJ-7721 was processed prior to invoice generation for the 7/29 billing run. If not, please issue a credit memo or corrected invoice and provide the credit memo ID.
- If the adjustment exists in AWS records but didn't flow to the invoicing pipeline, confirm ETA for corrective action.
- Provide any marketplace ticket reference so our customer can reconcile on their side.

We're happy to provide additional log extracts from Redwood's runtime if that helps. For speed, here's a short reconciliation summary we will accept as sufficient for AR: credit memo ID + corrected invoice PDF. We have a DocuSign link ready for Acme to confirm acceptance of the corrected invoice (https://docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF123456).

Thanks in advance — please reply with the marketplace ticket ID and timeline.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142
